C-RELEASE-REWRITE-BOUNDARY.Summary: Let the strict previous-release boundary of tools/release-readiness.mjs prove a release whose following history was rewritten: previousRelease.commit and previousRelease.tree keep proving the real annotated tag target and tree, previousRelease.bootstrapSha keeps proving ancestry and stays the commit-accounting origin, and a new previousRelease.historyRewrite field ({ date, deltaPaths }) proves the tag-to-bootstrap delta exactly while confining it to non-product paths; the bootstrapSha-equals-commit and the same-tree bootstrap behaviors stay unchanged.
C-RELEASE-REWRITE-BOUNDARY.Problem: Main history was rewritten after v2.8.2 shipped (the local reflog records the rewritten main fetched as a forced update on 2026-10-29), so no commit reachable from main carries the v2.8.2 tag tree (fcc46b7ba481d886d3e3d497af634337246c12f7; verified 2026-11-22). Because validateStrictRepositoryState requires previousRelease.bootstrapSha to resolve to a commit whose tree equals previousRelease.tree and to be an ancestor of the payload, train 2.9.x-next can never pass strict validation in Frozen (MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID, bootstrap=not-ancestor) and can never reach Ready, even though its nearest current-history base commit (16a4a47ed723740e330e44cf448bcbada766882c, PR #63, itself an ancestor of main) carries product paths byte-equal to the tag and an 81-path delta confined to site/ (72), tests/ (8) and .github/workflows/site.yml (1).

Goals.Goal: Equal and same-tree cases unchanged: when previousRelease.bootstrapSha equals previousRelease.commit, or when its tree equals previousRelease.tree, the strict proof is byte-identical to today — the bootstrapSha tree must equal previousRelease.tree ('tree=drift') and no previousRelease.historyRewrite field may be present; its presence is rejected.

Rewrite case: when previousRelease.bootstrapSha differs from previousRelease.commit and its tree differs from previousRelease.tree, require previousRelease.historyRewrite = { date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', deltaPaths: [sorted repository-relative paths] } and prove that `git diff --name-only <commit> <bootstrapSha>` equals deltaPaths exactly (same paths, same count, same order); any divergence fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID rewrite=delta-drift.

Product confinement: no deltaPaths entry may start with a product prefix (src/, src-tauri/, static/, mark-quicklook/) or equal a product file (package.json, package-lock.json, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml); any such entry fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID rewrite=product-drift, and the prefix and file lists are named constants of the tool.

Every other boundary and accounting fact stays untouched: the recorded commit must keep matching the real tag target (rev-parse tag^{commit}), previousRelease.tree must keep matching the tag tree, bootstrapSha must stay an ancestor of the payload ('bootstrap=not-ancestor'), commitAccounting.fromExclusive must stay equal to bootstrapSha, and exact rev-list commit accounting continues from bootstrapSha through the payload.

Constraints.Constraint: Existing failures keep their codes and messages verbatim: fail('MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID', 'tree=drift') still covers the tag tree check and the bootstrap tree check outside the rewrite case, and fail('MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID', 'bootstrap=not-ancestor') still covers ancestry. Missing or malformed historyRewrite when the bootstrapSha tree differs from previousRelease.tree, and any historyRewrite when that tree equals previousRelease.tree, fail with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID; historyRewrite.date follows the same YYYY-MM-DD real-calendar-date rule as testingProtocol dates.

Scope: only tools/release-readiness.mjs, tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js, one dated boundary note in docs/release-trains/README.md and the routed M-046/V-M-046 graph and verification records change. Tags are neither created, moved nor re-pointed; no history rewrite, no anchor tags, no merging the pre-rewrite line into main; docs/release-trains/2.9.x-next.json is not touched by this change.

Deterministic fixture tests only, in the file where the tool's strict-repository fixtures already live (tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js), with existing dependencies and no timeout or assertion weakening; the existing strictRepository fixture case (an empty bootstrap commit whose tree equals the tagged baseline tree) keeps passing unchanged, without any historyRewrite field.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No filling of previousRelease.bootstrapSha or previousRelease.historyRewrite in docs/release-trains/2.9.x-next.json; that bookkeeping is a separate train commit after the tool change lands.

No change to any other readiness gate: lifecycle transitions, membership, testing protocol, owner acceptance, seal span, screenshot freshness, required checks, payload/seal/tag/checkout identity, lane trains.
No release authorization, admission decision, version decision or publication action of any kind.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: With the bootstrapSha tree different from previousRelease.tree, a deltaPaths list exactly matching `git diff --name-only <commit> <bootstrapSha>` and free of product paths passes strict validation with all other evidence valid.
With the bootstrapSha tree equal to previousRelease.tree, including a bootstrapSha different from commit, strict validation passes without any historyRewrite field, exactly as today.
Any extra, missing or reordered path in deltaPaths fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID rewrite=delta-drift.
A deltaPaths entry starting with a product prefix or equal to a product file fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID rewrite=product-drift.

A bootstrapSha tree different from previousRelease.tree without a historyRewrite field, with a non-YYYY-MM-DD or non-calendar date, or with a non-list deltaPaths fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID.
A present historyRewrite field when the bootstrapSha tree equals previousRelease.tree fails with MT_RELEASE_PREVIOUS_BOUNDARY_INVALID.

Legacy negative controls keep failing exactly as today ('tree=drift' and 'bootstrap=not-ancestor'), and the checked-in Collecting train (bootstrapSha equal to commit, no historyRewrite) still validates unchanged.

AffectedAreas.Area: M-046: tools/release-readiness.mjs (validateStrictRepositoryState plus new named product-prefix/file constants and the module map entry), its deterministic fixtures in tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js, one dated boundary note in docs/release-trains/README.md, and the routed M-046/V-M-046 graph and verification records.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: New unit fixtures in tests/renderer/release-readiness.test.js cover these behaviors: matching product-free deltaPaths passes; extra/missing path fails rewrite=delta-drift; a product path fails rewrite=product-drift; missing historyRewrite at a differing bootstrap tree fails; the same-tree bootstrap passes without historyRewrite and a historyRewrite field there fails; 'tree=drift' and 'bootstrap=not-ancestor' negative controls still fail. The live checked-in Collecting train still validates. No real train, tag or history mutation.

Assumptions.Assumption: historyRewrite.date is validated for shape (YYYY-MM-DD real calendar date) only; no cross-check against commit timestamps is attempted.

Adding the optional previousRelease.historyRewrite field does not bump TRAIN_SCHEMA_VERSION ('1.0.0'): the schema string stays, and the field is tolerated only under the rewrite-case rule enforced above.
In the rewrite case the delta is never empty: two commits with different trees always differ in at least one path.
